basis: CIF NWE / Dated Brent physical proxy
note: Physical crude has decoupled from the screen. Brent futures settled Friday at $96.78 (down 3.9% on China-brokered diplomacy hopes, still +10% on the week; markets closed Saturday), but Dated Brent reached about $105.70 and North Sea Forties $108.77, with some grades near $110 — refiners paying a widening premium for barrels that are actually deliverable and suitable to run. The physical tightness reflects the compounding cascade: Hormuz at a controlled trickle (about three transits a day), the Houthis now striking Saudi refining and export infrastructure at Yanbu and Jazan (not only tankers), cargoes forced north through Suez and around the Cape of Good Hope, and Kazakhstan's CPC route still constrained. Editorial proxy, not a traded quote — indicative, and watch tanker-transit data over the rhetoric.
